name: IEC interconnection dependency (Z)
summary: Dependency label Zm showing an internal connection from one point of a symbol to every terminal labelled m.
description: Z dependency states that the affecting input or output is internally connected to every input or output labelled with the same number, which then takes its logic state. It lets a symbol show internal wiring without drawing it, for example an internal output that drives several internal inputs.

On device symbols, Z dependency often explains why an output appears to have the same state as an internal signal or why a pin also acts on another function. Drafters reproducing such symbols should keep the labels together.
Z dependency indicates logic state transfer only. It does not imply the connection is externally accessible or measurable.
readingNotes: Trace each Zm to every terminal labelled m.
Z labels describe internal connections, not external wiring.
drawingChecklist: Mark each connected terminal with m.
Do not use Z labels to stand in for external wiring.
distinction: X (transmission) dependency describes a bidirectional switch path controlled by the affecting input; Z is a fixed logical connection.
